title: encode/decode round trip fails for UUIDs with leading zero bits
body:
`ShortUUID.encode` in `shortuuid/main.py` pads short encodings on the
wrong end, so `decode(encode(u))` is not `u` whenever the encoded
number is shorter than the full length:

```python
>>> from uuid import UUID
>>> su = ShortUUID()
>>> su.decode(su.encode(UUID(int=1))) == UUID(int=1)
False   # expected True
```

The output is most-significant-digit first, so padding with the first
alphabet character must add leading (most significant) zeros, e.g.
`su.encode(UUID(int=0)) == "2" * 22` and `su.encode(UUID(int=1))`
ends with "3". Expected: `decode(encode(u)) == u` for every UUID and
every `pad_length`.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: int_to_string() pads on the least significant end.
